name: Engine R7: gaps for director films (cubic eases, pixel pivot, night and disco lighting)
description: Adds the three engine features the AEP converter needs to play director films faithfully: cubic-bezier eases written as cubic(x1,y1,x2,y2), a pixel pivot on every layer that overrides the 0..1 anchor, and the night and disco lighting presets the director uses. Nothing else.

userStories.title: cubic(x1,y1,x2,y2) eases: schema, pure solver, compiler
userStories.description: As a developer working on the AEP converter, I want to write a keyframe's bezier ease as cubic(x1,y1,x2,y2) so that director films keep their exact timing curves.
steps: Read engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md 'Keyframes → tweens', engine/src/schema/scalars.ts (EASE_PATTERN, EaseSchema) and engine/src/timeline/compile.ts (how ease is passed to GSAP).

Create engine/src/timeline/ease.ts exporting cubicBezier(x1, y1, x2, y2): (t: number) => number (CSS cubic-bezier semantics: Newton steps with a bisection fallback, x clamped to [0, 1], endpoints exact) and resolveEase(name: string): string | ((t: number) => number) that returns a function for 'cubic(a,b,c,d)' and the name unchanged otherwise.
Extend EASE_PATTERN in scalars.ts to accept cubic(x1,y1,x2,y2) with four decimal numbers (x1 and x2 in [0, 1], y any), spaces allowed after commas.
In compile.ts pass resolveEase(tween.ease) to GSAP instead of the raw string.
Create engine/src/timeline/ease.test.ts and add one case to the compile tests.
acceptanceCriteria: cubicBezier(0, 0, 1, 1)(0.3) is within 1e-6 of 0.3; cubicBezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1)(0.5) is within 1e-6 of 0.5; cubicBezier(0.42, 0, 1, 1)(0.25) is below 0.25
EaseSchema accepts 'cubic(0.42,0,0.58,1)' and 'cubic(0, 0, 0.58, 1)' and rejects 'cubic(2,0,1,1)' and 'cubic(0,0,1)'
A tween x 0 -> 100 over 1 s with ease 'cubic(0.42,0,0.58,1)' compiled on a clock reads 50 (within 1e-6) at seek 0.5 and the same value after seeking 0.9, 0, 0.5
All existing timeline tests pass unchanged
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Pixel pivot on every layer, overriding the 0..1 anchor
userStories.description: As a developer working on the AEP converter, I want to give a layer's anchor in pixels so that director layers rotate and scale about the same point as in After Effects without knowing the measured text size.
steps: Read engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md 'Base transform' and engine/docs/03-stage-2d.md 'Base transform', then engine/src/schema/layers2d.ts (LayerBaseShape) and engine/src/core/transform.ts (applyBaseTransform, setAnchor).
Add optional pivot: [number, number] (pixels in the layer's own space) to LayerBaseShape; it applies to every layer type including three.

In transform.ts make setAnchor(content, anchor, size, pivot?) put content at (-pivot[0], pivot[1], 0) when a pivot is given and keep the anchor rule otherwise; applyBaseTransform takes the layer's pivot.
Update every caller (stage2d nodes and threeNode, including the text node when it re-applies the anchor after a redraw) to pass layer.pivot.
Add tests to engine/src/core/transform.test.ts and to one node test.
acceptanceCriteria: applyBaseTransform for { x: 960, y: 540, pivot: [192, 336], anchor: [0.5, 0.5] } and size 384x672 gives content.position (-192, 336, 0) and display.position (960, -540, 0)
Without pivot the existing anchor test still gives content.position (-20, 20, 0)
A layer with pivot [0, 0] parses; pivot with three numbers fails with a path ending in .pivot
All existing engine tests pass
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: night and disco lighting presets
userStories.description: As a developer working on the AEP converter, I want the director's night and disco lighting presets in the three layer so that its 3D scenes keep their mood.
steps: Read engine/src/three/build/lighting.ts (LIGHTING_PRESETS and how a preset becomes a rig) and engine/src/schema/layer3d.ts (LIGHTING_PRESETS enum), and tmp/reacthub-pixitweenjs/src/components/AepComposition/model3d/lighting.ts plus tmp/reacthub-pixitweenjs/src/components/AepComposition/stage3d/ for any night or disco values.

Add 'night' (cool blue key at low intensity, dim fill, strong cold rim, environment none) and 'disco' (magenta key, cyan fill, warm rim, environment room) to both lists, porting the library's numbers when they exist and saying in notes where the numbers came from.
Add tests to engine/src/three/build/lighting.test.ts for both presets (rig has key, fill, rim, ambient; colours as defined).
acceptanceCriteria: resolveLightingConfig('night', {}) and resolveLightingConfig('disco', {}) return configs and createLightingRig builds four lights for each
A three layer with lighting { preset: 'night' } parses and its environment defaults to 'none'
All existing lighting and scene tests pass
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

metadata.standingRule: Engine PRD. Everything is offline and free: unit tests in vitest (jsdom project) and browser checks on the engine lab pages. The director app is not changed.
guardrails: Work offline. The only network use allowed is `npm install`. Tests never fetch; browser checks load assets from web/public.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Read engine/docs/README.md and the spec doc the story names before writing code. The spec is the contract: if it is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in notes.

Porting is allowed: read tmp/reacthub-pixitweenjs/src (a read-only copy of the library, inside this repo) and copy what engine/docs/port-map.md says. Never edit anything under tmp/. Every ported file starts with `// Ported from reacthub-pixitweenjs <path> (MIT).` and is cleaned up to strict TypeScript.
No `@ts-nocheck` and no `@ts-ignore` under engine/. `@ts-expect-error` only with a reason on the same line.

engine/ is Three.js + GSAP only: it must not import from web/, server/, shared/, `reacthub-pixitweenjs`, `pixi.js`, `pixi-filters`, `@pixi/*` or `@react-three/*`. Only the web stub files listed in metadata.sharedEdits may import engine/.

Do not touch the director app: nothing under server/, shared/, web/src/ (except the stub files under web/ listed in metadata.sharedEdits) or the existing e2e/ specs. Config files only as listed in metadata.sharedEdits.
Everything you build goes under engine/ (src/, fixtures/, lab/, e2e/, docs/). Edit only the files named in the story's steps and their tests, plus the small edits listed in metadata.sharedEdits.

Determinism: no Math.random, Date.now or performance.now in anything that affects pixels; no GSAP `overwrite`, no `immediateRender: true`, no infinite `repeat` (engine/docs/02-timeline.md, determinism rules).
jsdom has no 2D canvas context and no WebGL: unit-test pure logic and object construction; check drawing in the browser. Never weaken a test to make it pass.
Do not add a dependency the spec does not name (`postprocessing` and `@types/three` are already declared).

Debug output and screenshots go to debug/engine/ (gitignored). For a browser check use the dev server the owner runs on http://localhost:5173 (do not start another on a different port); if it is not running, run `npm run engine:e2e` instead.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements or test output.

`npm test` has 11 known failures outside engine/ (10 in scripts/preflight/docs.test.ts, 1 in web/src/authoring-agreement.test.tsx). They are not yours: do not edit those files. The `npm test` gate passes when no other test fails; also run `npx vitest run engine` and it must be fully green.

R1 is done: engine/ is Three-only. MotionNode (engine/src/core/types.ts) has `display` (layer transform) and `content` (the meshes, offset by the anchor); NodeContext has `renderer`. Effects live in engine/src/effects (EFFECTS, registerEffect, buildEffectChain, setEffectChainFactoryForTests).

The dev server on http://localhost:5173 is owner-run and shared: never kill, restart or stop it (no kill/pkill/lsof-kill on vite or port 5173). If it is down, use headless Chromium against `npx vite --config web/vite.config.ts --port 5180 --strictPort` started and stopped by you, and only that one.
Do not use GSAP CustomEase or any GSAP plugin; a cubic bezier is a small pure solver in engine/src/timeline/ease.ts.

ui: Verify in the browser: with the dev server on http://localhost:5173 (owner-run; else `npm run engine:e2e` once it exists), open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, save a screenshot to debug/engine/, and record what you saw in `notes`
